n1b9260a7c91.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: India – mainly structural and disguised unemployment
Developed countries – mainly structural and disguised unemployment
n1b9260a7c91.x: India's unemployment is mainly structural and disguised, while developed countries mainly face cyclical, demand-deficient unemployment.

nindian-economy-33-6.s: A recent graduate searching for a first job is an example of which type of unemployment?
nindian-economy-33-6.x: Frictional unemployment arises during the transition into or between jobs, as with a graduate seeking a first job.

n02cde4e96f0.s: Which of the following is a structural cause of unemployment in India's secondary sector?
o: Abundant job creation in labour-intensive industries
Slow infrastructure and delays in official paperwork
n02cde4e96f0.x: Slow infrastructure and paperwork delays are identified structural impediments; expansion of labour-intensive manufacturing would reduce unemployment, and MSMEs have been neglected.

n91fa1af78a5.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: UPS – employed if worked 90 days or more in 365 days
UPS – employed if worked 183 days or more in 365 days
UPS – employed if worked 273 days or more in 365 days
n91fa1af78a5.x: UPS uses a 365-day reference period and counts a person employed for the major part of it, generally 183 days or more; CWS uses a 7-day period.

nc412b5f0d0b.s: CWS unemployment rates exceed UPSS rates mainly because the 7-day reference period captures:
nc412b5f0d0b.x: The short 7-day CWS reference period picks up seasonal unemployment, so CWS rates are higher than UPSS rates.

n78c1e54093e.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Jobless growth – term coined by Arthur Lewis
Near-zero employment elasticity – rapid job creation
Jobless growth – term coined in the 1950s
Jobless growth – term coined by Nick Perna
n78c1e54093e.x: The term 'jobless growth' was coined by Nick Perna in the early 1990s; near-zero elasticity means output grows with little job growth.

nd10d0b55a5e.s: Agriculture accounts for about what share of rural employment in India?
nd10d0b55a5e.x: Agriculture accounts for about 57% of rural employment, while services account for 62.0% of urban employment.

n62dd52670d8.s: India's post-1991 growth was NOT sufficiently concentrated in which activity?
n62dd52670d8.x: Post-1991 growth was led by capital-intensive IT and finance and was not concentrated in labour-intensive manufacturing, so jobs lagged.

n2d7f30c2b7a.s: For 2025, India's urban Female LFPR was about:
n2d7f30c2b7a.x: In 2025 the Female LFPR was about 40% overall, 45.9% in rural areas and only 27.7% in urban areas.

n909f2f8d90d.s: The Labour Bureau's Quarterly Employment Survey covers establishments with 10 or more workers in how many sectors?
n909f2f8d90d.x: The QES covers establishments with 10 or more workers across nine sectors.

new.s: Farm labourers who stay idle in the off-season months face which type of unemployment?
new.x: Seasonal unemployment arises from predictable seasonal shifts in demand, as in farm labour during the off-season.

new.s: Under PLFS, open unemployment is higher in:
new.x: PLFS shows higher open unemployment in urban areas; in AP rural was 3.4% and urban 5.9% (2024-25).

new.s: Hiring halted because of rigid layoff rules and high minimum wages is an example of which unemployment?
new.x: Institutional unemployment arises from labour laws, high minimum wages and union rules.

new.s: Unemployment caused by depression in an economy is called:
new.x: A fall in aggregate demand during recession or depression causes cyclical unemployment (APPSC 2019).

new.s: Cyclical unemployment is linked with which phase of the business cycle?
new.x: Cyclical unemployment arises when aggregate demand falls in a recession and firms lay off workers to cut costs.

new.s: Which type of unemployment is short-term, arises from the time lag in searching for jobs and exists even at full employment?
new.x: Frictional (search) unemployment is short-term and normal, existing even at full employment.

new.s: A labour-intensive economy turning capital-intensive is most likely to cause:
new.x: Structural unemployment is long-term and arises from skill-job mismatch caused by changes in technology or demand.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about frictional and structural unemployment:
1. Frictional unemployment is short-term.
2. Structural unemployment needs reskilling or reform.
3. Frictional unemployment disappears at full employment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Frictional is short-term and structural is deep-rooted needing reskilling; frictional unemployment exists even at full employment, so 3 is wrong.

new.s: Automation in manufacturing and AI in services are expected to reduce demand mainly for:
new.x: Technological unemployment from automation and AI mainly hits low-skilled, routine jobs.

new.s: Technological unemployment is mainly found in:
new.x: Technological unemployment, a subtype of structural, is predominant in manufacturing and routine services.

new.s: Persons able and willing to work but having no job at all are in:
new.x: Open unemployment means being able and willing to work with no job at all.

new.s: Working fewer than the normal hours is known as:
new.x: Visible underemployment means fewer than normal hours; invisible underemployment is full-time work at very low income.

new.s: The labour force counts only which kind of unemployment?
new.x: Only involuntary unemployment (willing at the going wage but no job) is counted in the labour force.

new.s: A.W. Phillips showed the inverse relation between unemployment and inflation in:
new.x: A.W. Phillips presented the inverse unemployment-inflation relation in 1958.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Milton Friedman – natural rate of unemployment
new.x: Friedman is linked with the natural rate; Okun links unemployment with output, Phillips with inflation, and the vertical long-run curve is Friedman-Phelps.

new.s: As per PLFS 2025, the unemployment rate for Gen Z (15-26) was:
new.x: Gen Z (15-26) unemployment was 11.9%; 14.8% was for youth aged 18-29.

new.s: What share of India's tertiary-educated youth are NEET (not in employment, education or training)?
new.x: About 40.1% of tertiary-educated youth are NEET; 29.4% is their unemployment rate.

new.s: The main cause of educated unemployment in India is:
new.x: Educated unemployment is an urban phenomenon caused by a mismatch between curriculum and industry needs.

new.s: India's projected skilled-labour surplus by 2030 is about:
new.x: India is a labour-surplus economy with a projected skilled-labour surplus of about 245.3 million by 2030.

new.s: About what share of India's workforce is informal?
new.x: About 90% of India's workforce is informal, one of the causes behind its unemployment problem.

new.s: Under the CDS approach, a person is counted as employed for the day if he or she worked for:
new.x: CDS uses a half-day unit; working 4 or more hours counts as employed for the day.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the 183-day criterion:
1. It is the UPS 'major time' threshold.
2. It separates Census main workers from marginal workers.
3. The Census approach is one of the NSS status approaches.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: 183 days marks both UPS major time and the Census main-worker line, but the Census is not an NSS approach.

new.s: Which identity links the three labour indicators?
new.x: The worker population ratio equals LFPR multiplied by (1 − UR).

new.s: Unemployed persons as a percentage of the total population is called:
new.x: PU divides the unemployed by population, while UR divides them by the labour force.

new.s: The first annual PLFS report, for 2017-18, was released in:
new.x: PLFS was launched in April 2017 and its first annual report (2017-18) came out in May 2019.

new.s: From January 2025, PLFS began releasing which estimates?
new.x: The 2025 revamp added monthly all-India CWS estimates and extended quarterly estimates to rural areas.

new.s: In 2019, the CSO and NSSO were merged to form the:
o: Standing Committee on Labour Force Statistics
new.x: In 2019 the CSO and NSSO merged into the National Statistical Office (NSO).

new.s: As per PLFS 2019-20, the unemployment rate (UPSS) was:
new.x: PLFS 2019-20 put UR at 4.8% (APPSC 2022); 6.1% was for 2017-18.

new.s: The PLFS 2025 (calendar year) unemployment rate was:
new.x: PLFS 2025 gave a UR of 3.1%, down from 3.6% in 2022.

new.s: Which was the last quinquennial NSS employment-unemployment round?
new.x: The 68th round (2011-12) was the last quinquennial round before PLFS.

new.s: The Labour Bureau, which conducts the EUS and QES, was set up in:
new.x: The Labour Bureau (1920) under the Ministry of Labour and Employment conducts the EUS and QES.

new.s: CMIE's monthly unemployment data come from its:
new.x: CMIE is a private body that runs the monthly CPHS with a larger sample and different method.

new.s: The Dantwala Committee on unemployment estimates was set up in:
new.x: The Dantwala Committee was set up in 1970; the Bhagwati Committee followed in 1973.

new.s: In PLFS, Andhra Pradesh's urban unemployment rate (usual status) was about:
new.x: AP's urban rate was 5.9% against a rural rate of 3.4% and an overall 4.1%.

new.s: The unemployment rate of urban female youth in Andhra Pradesh, as per PLFS, was:
new.x: Urban female youth in AP had an unemployment rate of 29.1%; 22.7% and 15.5% were urban and rural youth rates.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Andhra Pradesh in PLFS 2023-24?
o: AP's unemployment rate was above the national rate
Urban youth unemployment exceeded rural youth unemployment
new.x: AP's male rate was 4.3% and female 3.7%, so female unemployment did not exceed male.

new.s: Critics say the CWS measure misses which phenomenon?
new.x: CWS counts 1 hour a week as employed, masking underemployment and missing circular migration.

new.s: About how many people enter India's job market every year?
new.x: About 12 million people enter India's job market every year while formal jobs lag.

new.s: Between 2011 and 2023, contract workers' share of factory employment rose to:
new.x: Direct factory employment fell from 61% to 47%, while contract workers rose to 42%.

new.s: Informal sector enterprises are unincorporated private enterprises with fewer than:
new.x: The informal sector consists of unincorporated private enterprises owned by individuals or households with fewer than 10 workers.

new.s: The National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (NCEUS), set up in 2004, was chaired by:
new.x: NCEUS was set up in 2004 under the chairmanship of Arjun Sengupta.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about informality in India:
1. Nearly 82% of the workforce is in the informal sector.
2. Nearly 90% of workers are informally employed.
3. Informal employment exists only in the informal sector.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: IER 2024 puts 82% in the informal sector and 90% informally employed; informal employment can exist in any sector.

new.s: Andhra Pradesh's rural informal share of employment (2024-25) was:
new.x: AP's informal share was 62.3% in rural and 45.6% in urban areas, about 55% overall.

new.s: According to the India Employment Report 2024, casual employment's share in 2022 was:
new.x: In 2022 self-employment was 55.8%, casual 22.7% and regular wage/salaried 21.5%.

new.s: What share of Gen Z workers have any social security?
new.x: Only 20.1% of Gen Z workers have any social security, and only 14.2% have a formal contract.

new.s: Which sector is the largest employer in the Labour Bureau's Quarterly Employment Survey?
new.x: Manufacturing is the largest QES employer (38.5%, Jan-Mar 2022), followed by education (21.7%).

new.s: Which of the following is NOT among the nine sectors of the Quarterly Employment Survey?
new.x: The QES covers nine non-farm sectors such as manufacturing, construction, trade, education and health; agriculture is not one of them.

new.s: The PLFS Female LFPR (15+) for 2017-18 was:
new.x: Female LFPR was 23.3% in 2017-18, rising to 32.5% in 2020-21 and 41.7% in 2023-24.

new.s: Rural women accounted for about what share of the rise in female workers from 2017-18 to 2023-24?
new.x: Rural women made up 80% of the rise, largely through subsistence farming and unpaid family work.

new.s: The four Labour Codes consolidate how many central labour laws?
new.x: The four Labour Codes consolidate 29 central labour laws and came into force from 21 Nov 2025.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four Labour Codes?
new.x: The four codes are on Wages, Social Security, Industrial Relations and OSH; there is no separate code on gig workers.

new.s: The e-Shram portal was launched on:
new.x: e-Shram, the national database of unorganised workers, was launched on 26 August 2021.

new.s: Each worker registered on the e-Shram portal gets a:
new.x: Every e-Shram registrant receives a 12-digit Universal Account Number.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the e-Shram portal:
1. It is a national database of unorganised workers.
2. It has about 31.89 crore registrations.
3. It covers most of India's gig workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: e-Shram has about 31.89 crore registrations of unorganised workers, but most gig workers are outside it.

new.s: As per PLFS, Andhra Pradesh's Female LFPR for persons aged 15+ was:
new.x: AP's 15+ Female LFPR was 44.8% against India's 41.7%; 35.8% is AP's all-age figure.

new.s: Employment elasticity is low when:
o: Output grows with little rise in employment
Each unit of growth creates many jobs
new.x: Employment elasticity is % change in employment over % change in output; a low value signals jobless growth.
